verdicts.correction: The quotes are exact; the ellipsis only drops 'in the same repository'. The FAQ's doubt, though, is wider than 'which version'. It is whether the GPL's permissions reach the source files at all. If they did not, the fallback would be no licence at all, not a permissive one. So 'no non-GPL route' holds, but the real risk is having no permission at all. Second point: under #TranslateCode the Kotlin ports must carry 'the same versions' as upstream. If Rouxtine treats upstream as GPL-3.0 (only), the ported files should be marked GPL-3.0-only. GPL-3.0-or-later is safe only for Rouxtine's own new files, or for ported files once onionhoney states 'or later'. Asking him to add an explicit statement removes the doubt; per the FAQ it 'eliminates all doubt'.

Without such a statement, it's not entirely clear that the permissions in the license really apply to any particular source file. An explicit statement saying that eliminates all doubt.'

verdicts.correction: The cited texts are accurate. But no GPL or FAQ text says outright that premium in-app purchases are 'allowed'; that is inferred from s.4 and from the absence of any prohibition. Any premium gate must therefore stay a purely technical feature: no EULA or ToS term, and no technical or legal barrier to removing it. The s.3 waiver (LICENSE:187-193) is more direct authority than FAQ #DRMProhibited, which is about building DRM with GPL code.

The Android SDK License (s.3.4) forbids redistributing 'any part of the SDK' and contains no express grant to ship SDK parts inside apps. The only licence Google declares for the billing AAR therefore does not, on its face, authorise bundling it in an APK; permission is implied by Google's own requirement to use it. Source: https://developer.android.com/studio/terms

FAQ #WhatCaseIsOutputGPL acknowledges that 'some programs, particularly video games, can have artwork/audio that is licensed separately from the underlying GPLed game'. This is FSF-recognised support for separately licensed standalone assets (license-55 / option C), but it does not reach Compose theme code, which is Kotlin. Source: https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.html#WhatCaseIsOutputGPL

GPLv3 s.4 also expressly allows that 'you may offer support or warranty protection for a fee' (LICENSE:205-206). That is a GPL-sanctioned revenue line (paid coaching, support or priority help) that the options list omits; whether Play Billing applies to it is a Play-policy question. Source: https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.txt
